source_text: וְ/אָנֹכִ֤י תִרְגַּ֨לְתִּי֙ לְ/אֶפְרַ֔יִם קָחָ֖/ם עַל זְרֽוֹעֹתָ֑י/ו וְ/לֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ כִּ֥י רְפָאתִֽי/ם־׃
english_snapshot: Yet it was I who taught Ephraim to walk[a], taking them in my arms, but they did not know that I healed them.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'taking them in his arms'; the Masoretic Text has a difficult third-person form/suffix in this clause. Many interpreters understand the sense as continuing the LORD's first-person speech: 'I took them in my arms.'

source_text: וָ/יָּ֤שַׂר אֶל מַלְאָךְ֙ וַ/יֻּכָ֔ל בָּכָ֖ה וַ/יִּתְחַנֶּן ל֑/וֹ בֵּֽית אֵל֙ יִמְצָאֶ֔/נּוּ וְ/שָׁ֖ם יְדַבֵּ֥ר עִמָּֽ/נוּ־־־׃
english_snapshot: He strove with the angel and prevailed[a]; he wept and sought his favor. At Bethel he found him[b], and there he spoke with us—

signals.text: Hebrew 'with us'; some understand 'with him,' smoothing the shift in person. The main text preserves the Masoretic reading.

source_text: וְ/עַתָּ֣ה יוֹסִ֣פוּ לַ/חֲטֹ֗א וַ/יַּעְשׂ֣וּ לָ/הֶם֩ מַסֵּכָ֨ה מִ/כַּסְפָּ֤/ם כִּ/תְבוּנָ/ם֙ עֲצַבִּ֔ים מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חָרָשִׁ֖ים כֻּלֹּ֑/ה לָ/הֶם֙ הֵ֣ם אֹמְרִ֔ים זֹבְחֵ֣י אָדָ֔ם עֲגָלִ֖ים יִשָּׁקֽוּ/ן׀׃
english_snapshot: And now they keep on sinning: they make cast images for themselves from their silver, idols made according to their own skill—all of it the work of craftsmen. Of them they say[a], “Those who sacrifice human beings kiss calves[b][c].”

signals.text: Or, 'Let those who sacrifice kiss calves.' This takes 'human' generically and reads the final verb with jussive-like force; the Masoretic form is more naturally indicative, 'kiss.'
